transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jamie Clarke (Redwood AE), Sam Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (BlueWave CTO), Marcus Lee (BlueWave ML), Ana Gutierrez (BlueWave Data), Ethan Cole (BlueWave Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in — focus on model pinning and catalog comparison. Quick review of benchmarks (docs shared - link to spreadsheet), decision to run extended quantized tests, agreement to confirm target SLAs for Dedicated sizing.

--- Transcript Body ---
[00:00] Jamie Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's a busy week. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here. Marcus and Ana are on from infra and data. Ethan as well.
[00:10] Jamie Clarke: Great. Sam, you wanna kick off with the benchmark highlights?
[00:13] Sam Nguyen: Yeah sure, uh we ran the week-long microbench across three model families — the small redwood family, a mid-sized open model (we labeled it rwd-rl-1.3b for shorthand), and a larger 7b-ish variant from a community catalog. Results are in the sheet we shared, link in chat. Key points: hosted runs had consistent 95th pct around 420ms for the 1.3b baseline, the 7b was 700-850ms depending on prompt length, and when we enabled 4-bit quantization we saw a 20-35% throughput improvement but a slight increase in tail variance on some sequences.
[01:15] Marcus Lee: When you say tail variance, is that like occasional spikes or sustained?
[01:18] Sam Nguyen: Mostly occasional spikes — we suspect it's interaction with kv cache warmups on user sessions. Some of the longer context prompts saw a rollback to CPU-path for one replica during the test, that added a few outliers.
[01:30] Ana Gutierrez: Could that be because the k-v cash — sorry k-v cache — wasn't warmed, or is it more kernel selection?
[01:35] Sam Nguyen: Prob both. The profiler shows warmup thrash, and kernel selection sometimes flips when sequence length changes mid-request. We're adding a prefix caching config for the next run.
[01:45] Priya Rao: For us latency is top priority. Our product team wants 95th under 500ms for typical 256-token prompts. Cost is secondary but still important — we were aiming to stay within ~0.8x of our current CPU cluster spend.
[01:58] Jamie Clarke: Good context. So tradeoff is clear: the quantized 4-bit gives cost wins but we need to validate 95th pct. Sam — can we pin a specific model variant for the pilot so we avoid noisy rollouts?
[02:08] Sam Nguyen: Yes. Our recommendation is to pin to rwd-rl-1.3b@v1.7-quant4 for the initial pilot on hosted, and run a parallel Dedicated test on rwd-rl-1.3b@v1.6 (non-quant) to measure production parity. If the quant4 shows stable tails in the larger 1k request run, we can promote it. Fallback policy would route to the non-quantized v1.6 if the 95th pct goes over the configured SLO more than 3% of traffic in a 10m window.
[02:40] Ethan Cole: That rollback/fallback rule — is it automatic in Redwood or do you want us to handle it?
[02:44] Sam Nguyen: We can set automated routing policies — it's a built-in capability. You'd give us the SLO threshold and fallback target, and we wire the route. We'll demo the policy in the Dedicated sizing session.
[02:57] Priya Rao: Question on data residency: our compliance team requires that inference logs for EU customers stay in-region. If we go Hosted for pilot, will logs be segmented?
[03:05] Jamie Clarke: Yes, we can scope region pinning for logs and model execution. For pilot we'll keep EU workloads in eu-central region. For Private or Dedicated we can do customer-managed VPC and KMS.
[03:15] Marcus Lee: On the Dedicated sizing — how many GPUs would you estimate for our qps? We sent sample traces, right?
[03:20] Sam Nguyen: We have the sample but we need the 95th target confirmed. Based on current traffic sample and 95th=500ms, likely 2x A10G-class or 1x higher-end instance for steady state with burst policies. But we'll give exact numbers after the 1k quantized run.
[03:37] Ana Gutierrez: Is there a measurable difference in output quality when moving to quant4? We've seen hallucination increases before with aggressive quant.
[03:44] Sam Nguyen: Good callout. In our small eval set we saw negligible quality delta for a factual retrieval task, but for longer generation prompts there were sporadic tokenization artifacts — probably due to fp->int mapping. We'll run a quality regression suite with your eval prompts as part of the 1k run.
[03:59] Priya Rao: Also want to know about audit logs / SOC2. We're going to need SOC2 evidence and e-discovery for the pilot.
[04:05] Maya Patel: We have the security pack — Jamie will share the SOC2 and ISO docs + our standard AIA by EOD. We can redact the pilot-level logs when needed and provide retention controls.
[04:18] Jamie Clarke: I'll send the security pack link and the benchmark spreadsheet. Sam, can you enumerate the exact config you'll test next?
[04:24] Sam Nguyen: Sure: 1) rwd-rl-1.3b@v1.7-quant4 hosted (1k sample) with prefix caching enabled; 2) rwd-rl-1.6-nonquant dedicated sim (1k sample) to measure parity; 3) regressions on your 50 eval prompts for hallucination checks. We'll capture per-request latency, p50/p95/p99, and token-level quality diffs.
[04:40] Ethan Cole: How will we share results? Spreadsheet + traces?
[04:43] Sam Nguyen: Spreadsheet with histograms, link to perf traces (lightweight pprof-like traces), and a small summary doc. We'll also post the route config JSON in the shared drive — it's not a prod config but shows fallback rules.
[04:55] Priya Rao: I'm a bit concerned about the rollback frequency threshold — if it triggers too often it could create jitter. Can we put a cooldown?
[05:01] Sam Nguyen: Absolutely. We typically set a 5-minute cooldown after a rollback and require the ping rate to be below threshold for two consecutive windows before reverting. We'll add that to the policy example.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: Any competitor risk we should be aware of? We briefly evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI earlier. OpenAI's managed endpoints had lower tail for our shorter prompts but cost was higher. Anthropic had good safety filters but didn't fit our budget. So Redwood's balance looks promising but need to validate dedicated numbers.
[05:30] Jamie Clarke: Good. To recap — agreement to run the extended quant4 bench, pin initial pilot to rwd-rl-1.3b@v1.7-quant4 on hosted with automatic fallback to v1.6-nonquant, run dedicated parity test, and share security docs. Next call we'll review results and sizing.
[05:47] Priya Rao: That sounds good. Can we get the bench and security docs this week?
[05:51] Jamie Clarke: Yes — security pack and benchmark sheet by EOD tomorrow. Sam will run the 1k by Thursday and attach results.
[05:59] Ana Gutierrez: One more ops nit — if we pin to a quant variant, how do we handle model version rollbacks if upstream model weights change?
[06:06] Sam Nguyen: We version pin via the catalog ID and commit hash, so upstream changes don't auto-swap. Rollouts are explicit — you opt-in to model upgrades or we can set a canary percentage. If an upstream push happens, you remain pinned until you authorize the update.
[06:22] Ethan Cole: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:25] Jamie Clarke: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. See you next week.

--- End Transcript ---
